newsitem.title: SPAIN: RALLYING-MCRAE LEADS SUBARU 1-2 VICTORY IN CATALUNYA.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MCRAE LEADS SUBARU 1-2 VICTORY IN CATALUNYA.

text.p: Britain's Colin McRae triumphed over Italian team mate Piero Liatti in the Catalunya Rally on Wednesday to give Subaru first and second places and victory in the manufacturers' championship.

Ex-world champion McRae started the last leg of the 1,368-kilometre event only three seconds behind former European champion Liatti and remorselessly increased the pressure to snatch the lead on the penultimate stage.
A measured performance gave him his third championship victory of the season.
The seven-second margin made him the first British driver to win the rally and salvaged second place in the final points table after a mixed season in which he has crashed as often as he won.
"It was a bit of a close fight. There was never any breathing space, but it was a good day for me," the Scot said.

"After the year we've had it's good to win the last two rallies. The last stage was the worst. I slid a bit wide on one corner and I thought I was going to have another accident to add to this year's tally."
In the battle for third place, Belgium's Bruno Thiry held off fellow countryman Freddy Loix, despite a serious hydraulic problem with his Ford.
World champion Tommi Makinen of Finland made sure of fifth place, unable to match the leaders on asphalt roads that did not suit his Mitsubishi.
Catalunya marked the end of an era. Next year's championship, which starts in Monte Carlo in January, will be enlarged from nine to 14 rounds and feature radically modified cars.
